extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of church history, especially those interested in the Waldenses/Vaudois
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter from a historical narrative describing the organization, offices, missionary practice, persecutions, and communal life of the Vaudois (Waldenses). Aimed at conveying institutional rules and historical events rather than giving prescriptive modern guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synod composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Synod is the representative assembly of the Vaudois Church, and consists of all recognized pastors and certain laymen chosen by the parishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It 'takes cognizance of every matter affecting the welfare and duties of the church; it alters, adds, or abolishes all rules and regulations connected with its administration or discipline; it directs the course of theological study and admission to the ministry; it nominates the members of the table or any special bodies of commissioners for particular occasions; it superintends all evangelic work, whether in the valleys or its numerous mission stations in other places.' It now meets yearly (formerly met less often).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table (executive) composition and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: THE TABLE is the executive of the Vaudois Church, and consists of five members, the moderator, assistant moderator, and secretary being pastors, with two laymen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table is appointed by the synod from year to year, and is responsible to that body in respect of its operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for office of pastor
rubrics_metrics.description: To exercise the office of pastor a person must: (α) have attained the age of twenty-three, (β) have the requisite gifts for the work of the ministry, (γ) be of irreproachable character, (δ) receive a certificate from his university or other place of education, (ε) profess convictions in harmony with the doctrines and discipline of the Vaudois Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These points are decided by the table, in concert with the whole body of the pastors of the church. A pastor must be set apart by the laying on of hands. Additionally, a pastor is not allowed to have the sole care of a parish before he has reached the age of twenty-five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and characterization of evangelists
rubrics_metrics.description: Evangelists hold an office common to all evangelical churches (though under different titles such as catechist, reader, lay missionary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats the name and office as self-explanatory and does not provide further special qualification besides being part of evangelical ministry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elders: qualifications and election procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The elders are lay members of the church of well-known religious character, residing in the parish, and not receiving any benefit from the funds they may be called upon to administer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At an election of an elder for the first time he is required before installation to undergo an examination by a commission from the consistory of his own parish, assisted by a pastor from the nearest adjoining parish. The elder is chosen for life, unless he voluntarily resigns, or falls into a breach of church discipline, or becomes incapacitated by failing health; in the latter case he retains the title of honorary elder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deacons: qualifications, term, and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The deacons must have much the same qualifications as the elders. They are elected for five years, and their special work is the care of the sick and needy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes similarity of moral/character qualifications to elders and specifies a fixed term (five years) with clear charitable responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious observances and holy days
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to a zealous observance of the Lord's-day, the Waldensian Church pays a religious regard to Christmas-day, New-year's-day, Ascension-day, and Good Friday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good Friday is kept with great solemnity as a fast-day common to the whole Church of Christ; these days are singled out as maintained religiously by the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary funding and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: A portion of funds contributed by the church was assigned to the purpose of maintaining a body of pastors for the foreign work. These pastors being trained and set apart by the barbes for the work of the ministry were named by the synod for their special sphere of labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missionary appointments were organized and financed centrally; the synod directed appointments for foreign mission service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary training and deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of preparation for the ministry involved the learning by heart of the first and fourth gospels, the whole of the canonical epistles, and a large portion of the Old Testament. The missionaries to foreign churches generally remained abroad for two years. As a rule the synod despatched their missionaries two and two; one of the two was selected as more or less acquainted with the character of the places and persons they were about to visit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies memorization-based doctrinal preparation, paired deployment for mutual support, and typical mission duration (two years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary methods (disguise and tract distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: At times missionaries obtained access to higher classes in the character of pedlars: after displaying goods and making a sale, the pedlar would produce 'a pearl'—a small and meagre book (scripture) and quote portions of Scripture to those who would listen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes an intentional covert evangelistic method used to reach social groups otherwise inaccessible; includes an illustrative narrative and verse about offering the 'word of God' free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonization and external community organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Waldenses established colonies (e.g., in Apulia, Calabria, Liguria) where lords permitted them to settle on favourable terms; they built towns, maintained direct communion with brethren in the valleys, and the valleys supplied them with pastors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies were a strategy for spreading and maintaining the faith abroad and for protecting communities under pressure; ties to the valleys were maintained via visiting pastors and synodal support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripture translation and church building as signs of piety
rubrics_metrics.description: One sign of earnestness was the translation of the Holy Scriptures into French (out of the Romaunce dialect). A further proof of piety was shown in the erection of buildings for public worship (first temple at St. Lorenzo, A.D. 1535; additional temples by 1556).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of scriptures and construction of temples are presented as institutional indicators of evangelical zeal and public confession of faith.
